extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers looking up Snopes or fact-checking website practices
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of the fact-checking website Snopes, its history, editorial practices, ratings, controversies, and operational decisions — revealing standards and practices relevant to running and evaluating an online fact-checking site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide evidence for debunkings and confirmations
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes 'stressed the reference portion of the name Urban Legends Reference Pages, indicating that the intention is not merely to dismiss or confirm misconceptions and rumors but to provide evidence for such debunkings and confirmation as well.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging claims, present supporting sources and documentary evidence alongside the verdict; analyses should cite sources and reputable analyses to substantiate conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use explicit verdict labels when evidence is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, pages are generally marked 'undetermined' or 'unverifiable' when there is not enough evidence to either support or disprove a given claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not force a true/false verdict if evidence is lacking; adopt explicit intermediate labels (e.g., undetermined/unverifiable) and explain why the evidence does not suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply consistent, even-handed debunking standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes applies the same debunking standards to political urban legends regardless of whether complaints of bias come from left or right; external review (FactCheck.org) found sampled responses free from bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use uniform criteria across topics and political perspectives; document methods so external reviewers can assess impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify satire explicitly (add a 'Labeled Satire' rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes added a new rating called 'Labeled Satire' to identify satirical stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish satire from false factual claims by applying a dedicated label and explaining why the content is satirical to avoid misleading readers and incorrect fact-checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain methodology and make FAQs available
rubrics_metrics.description: The article references Snopes' 'Frequently Asked Questions' and statements such as 'How do I know the information you've presented is accurate?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish a clear methodology and FAQ that explains sourcing, verification processes, and how verdicts are reached so readers can judge reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial transparency and disclosure of funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Between 2016 and 2021 Snopes published a yearly summary detailing expenses and sources of income; the site disclosed funding streams such as advertising, GoFundMe, awards and partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly publish summaries of income and expenses and disclose major funding sources and partnerships so readers can assess potential conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate and remediate editorial misconduct (retractions, internal review, suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: After BuzzFeed News reported plagiarism by co-founder David Mikkelson, Snopes launched an internal review, retracted 60 articles, and suspended him from editorial duties during the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If misconduct is discovered, promptly investigate, publicly correct or retract affected content, and take personnel or governance actions to preserve editorial integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate readers about limits of internet authority and verification pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes assembled the 'Repository of Lost Legends' (T.R.O.L.L.) — fabricated tales intended to demonstrate the perils of over-reliance on the Internet as authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use illustrative examples and educational material to show readers how misinformation spreads and why critical scrutiny is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triangulate claims using multiple reputable sources and analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes that 'cited sources and numerous reputable analyses of its content confirm its accuracy' and references the site's practice of assembling evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm claims through independent, reputable sources and where possible present multiple lines of evidence rather than relying on a single source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure partnerships align with mission and community benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes ended its fact-checking partnership with Facebook, stating it needed to 'determine with certainty that our efforts to aid any particular platform are a net positive for our online community, publication and staff.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate platform or commercial partnerships for alignment with editorial mission and community impact; be prepared to end relationships that compromise independence or fail to benefit stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept user submissions but verify before publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Snopes grew to encompass a wide range of subjects and became a resource to which Internet users began submitting pictures and stories of questionable veracity; early site presentation included search results of user discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow user contributions as leads, but subject submitted claims to the same verification and sourcing standards before publishing fact-checks or verdicts.
